A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same F-FCI/F-PAG research. All 22 pages of v1 and 25 pages of v2, including figures, equations, proofs and experimental appendices, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix D report original synthetic causal-discovery experiments and gene-network inference from the Norman perturbation dataset.

after.justification: V2 retains the original simulation and gene-network results and adds selection-severity, nonlinearity and noise-family experiments in Appendix D.2.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, Step 2.3 adds a refinement using contrasts between two hard interventions to resolve circle-arrow ambiguities that v1 explicitly left unresolved. It also specifies hard-intervention contrasts for Type I path refinement. This changes the information used and the claimed recoverable orientations, while retaining the skeleton-learning and remaining orientation stages.

E1.justification: The causal-discovery task and Norman dataset remain unchanged. Appendix D.2 broadens synthetic input conditions to richer nonlinear mechanisms and Laplace/Gumbel noise, extending coverage beyond the existing uniform-noise experiments.

E2.justification: Both versions evaluate GIES, IGSP, UT-IGSP, JCI-GSP, FCI-INTERVEN and CDIS in the main comparisons. New Table 2 reuses FCI-INTERVEN for an additional stress test. GISL is newly discussed but is not evaluated as a comparator.

E3.justification: New protocols use 20-variable graphs with 5–6 selection variables and 2–3 latent confounders, and 15-variable graphs with expanded structural functions or alternative noise distributions. Original experimental settings and metrics are retained; these are additional protocols, not documented reruns under revised settings.

E4.justification: Appendix D.2 substantially extends the robustness analysis beyond the retained noise-magnitude and scalability studies. Tables 2–5 test stronger selection against FCI-INTERVEN, increased functional complexity, and sensitivity to heavy-tailed and asymmetric noise.

E5.justification: The existing ten-graph/ten-seed aggregation, 95% confidence intervals and Table 1 mean-and-variance reporting remain unchanged. Tables 2–5 also report ten-run aggregates with plus/minus values; no increased repetition count or new statistical estimation procedure is stated.

E6.justification: Tables 2–5 add substantial numerical evidence under new conditions. For example, Table 2's hard-intervention, n=2000 comparison reports precision of 64.2 versus 43.7 for FCI-INTERVEN, but recall of 66.4 versus 77.8. Figure 11 also replaces the illustrative inferred graph. Original benchmark curves, Table 1 and Figure 13 are retained; the added scores do not establish same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 adds an assumption that selection acts on at least two observed variables. Definitions 1/12 and new Remark 1 extend intervention indicators to comparisons between intervention environments. Theorem 3 broadens its square-mark soundness statement, and Appendix B revises the identification argument and completeness proof. These change formal scope and reasoning, although the soundness proof retains its earlier restrictive concluding sentence.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and central conclusion retain the same claims: explicitly model post-treatment selection, characterize FI-Markov equivalence through F-PAG, and provide a sound and complete F-FCI algorithm supported by synthetic and real-data experiments.

C2.justification: The biological interpretation shifts from repression-related FEV/CBFA2T3/SET hubs to QC-related explanations involving ZNF318, CDKN1C, CDKN1A and RREB1, despite retaining Figure 13. V2 adds interpretations of the stress tests and distinctions among three selection mechanisms. It removes the old circle-arrow limitation, retains the Type I/II limitation, and adds distinguishing biological constraints from post-treatment selection as an open problem.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 adds a Python implementation repository link absent from v1. Appendix D.2 documents the expanded function family and Laplace/Gumbel parameter sampling. Existing baseline implementation information, CI-test significance level and real-data processing details remain.

R1.justification: V2 adds Luo et al. (2025)/GISL and a focused Appendix E comparison of F-FCI with GISL and CDIS. It also replaces several biological references to support the revised gene interpretation. The broader related-work survey in Appendix C is retained.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence remain intact. V2 expands intervention explanations, inserts Appendix D.2, moves the real-data subsection to D.3, brings retained limitations into Section 6, and replaces Appendix E with discussion. Contact information and the conference header are also updated.

P2.justification: V2 adds a substantial set of tabulated robustness comparisons in Tables 2–5. It revises Figure 5(d), redraws Figure 8, and replaces and relocates Figure 11. Figures 6 and 10 correct the method legend from R-FCI to F-FCI while retaining their plotted results.

improvement.justification: The added stress tests make performance beyond uniform-noise settings more assessable, and the implementation link improves reproducibility information. These are useful gains over v1. However, the broader soundness statement remains incompletely reconciled with Appendix B, and the noise-robustness discussion underplays soft-intervention recall reductions in Tables 4–5. The evidence supports a limited overall improvement, not a demonstrated resolution of the central theoretical limitation.
